body.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_4\), on \(\mathcal E_N\) the fixed-target-weight cohort-mean PPML-imputation estimator obeys \(\sqrt N(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}-\theta_{\mathrm{PTT}})=h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\sqrt N(\overline Y-m)+o_P(1)\), with asymptotic variance \(h_{\mathrm{CM}}^{\prime}\Omega h_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
body.justification: This differentiates the cohort-mean comparator defined in the core and identifies the exact coefficient whose cycle projection governs its efficiency loss.
body.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Section 3.2.2, equations 3.13--3.14) instead fits untreated individual-observation fixed effects and aggregates individual counterfactual predictions; neither that paper nor Wooldridge (2023, Sections 2--3) provides this cohort-mean influence expansion under arbitrary within-unit covariance.
body.consumer: The expansion lets analysts compute the cohort-mean estimator's variance and its distance from the canonical bound without conflating it with an individual fixed-effects procedure.
